tweets.text: The public has lost trust in AI. @IrenaCronin and I write this newsletter every week. Public trust could become one of AI’s biggest challenges. People may push back if they think AI only helps big companies, wealthy investors, or government agencies. For AI to be accepted, people need to see that it helps workers, improves services, protects privacy, and benefits everyday users. Trust will depend on clear rules, honesty, and using AI to support people, not replace or control them. Read for free and please subscribe: unaligned.io

articles.content: Universal Manipulation Exoskeleton Universal Manipulation Exoskeleton Learning Compliant Whole-body Policies with Real-time Torque Feedback Litian Liang *, 1 , James (Jingxi) Xu *, 1, 2 , Xinda Qi 1 , Yujun Cai 1 , Houzhu Ding 1 , Luqi Wang 1 , Zhixin Sun 1 , Jyh-Herng Chow 1 , Ming Yang 1 , Mark Cutkosky 2 1 Ant Group, 2 Stanford University * Equal contribution Paper arXiv Video Code (coming soon) Data --> Teleoperator unsheathing a metal sword relying purely on real-time haptic torque feedback. Abstract For robots to work safely in household environments, they need to be compliant and react to torque and force feedback during contact. However, the majority of existing data collection pipelines still lack the ability to capture force and torque data for learning active compliant policies.
